title: Trig Identities
description: Reciprocal, Pythagorean, even/odd and cofunction identities; sum, difference, double- and half-angle formulas; product-to-sum; proof strategy.

cards.title: $\sec\theta$ is the reciprocal of which trig function?
cards.body:
$\cos\theta$: $\sec\theta = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}$.

Likewise $\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}$ and $\cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$.

Watch out: $\sec$ is not $\frac{1}{\sin}$.
Mnemonic: each reciprocal pair has exactly one "co": cos-**sec**, sin-**csc**, tan-**cot**.
cards.searchQuery: secant reciprocal of cosine identity

cards.title: Complete the Pythagorean identity: $1 + \cot^2\theta = \,?$
cards.body:
$\csc^2\theta$

Divide $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ through by $\sin^2\theta$ to get $1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta$. Dividing by $\cos^2\theta$ instead gives $\tan^2\theta + 1 = \sec^2\theta$.

Mnemonic: **tan** goes with **sec**, **cot** goes with **csc**.
cards.searchQuery: 1 plus cot squared equals csc squared identity

cards.title: If $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant II, what is $\cos\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{4}{5}$

$\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}$, so $\cos\theta = \pm\frac{4}{5}$. Cosine is negative in QII, so $\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}$.

Key idea: the identity gives the **size**; the quadrant picks the sign.
cards.searchQuery: find cosine from sine quadrant II Pythagorean identity

cards.title: Use even/odd identities to simplify $\sin(-\theta)\sec(-\theta)$.
cards.body:
$-\tan\theta$

$\sin$ is odd, so $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta$; $\sec$ is even, so $\sec(-\theta) = \sec\theta$. The product is $-\sin\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = -\tan\theta$.

Why: replacing $\theta$ by $-\theta$ flips the $y$-coordinate of the unit-circle point but not the $x$-coordinate.
Tip: only **cos** and **sec** are even; the other four are odd.
cards.searchQuery: even odd trig identities simplify sin(-theta) sec(-theta)

cards.title: Cofunction identity: $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \,?$
cards.body:
$\cot\theta$

Cofunctions of complementary angles are equal: $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cos\theta$, $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cot\theta$, $\sec\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \csc\theta$.

Why: in a right triangle, the leg opposite one acute angle is the leg adjacent to the other.
cards.searchQuery: cofunction identity tan pi/2 minus theta equals cot

cards.title: What is the standard strategy for proving a trig identity?
cards.body:
Transform **one side**, usually the more complicated one, step by step until it matches the other. You may also simplify each side separately to a common form.

Go-to moves: rewrite everything in $\sin$ and $\cos$, combine fractions, factor, use Pythagorean identities, or multiply by a conjugate such as $1 + \sin\theta$.

Watch out: never apply an operation across the equals sign; that assumes what you are trying to prove.
cards.searchQuery: strategy for proving trigonometric identities

cards.title: State the sum and difference formulas for $\sin(A \pm B)$ and $\cos(A \pm B)$.
cards.body:
$\sin(A \pm B) = \sin A\cos B \pm \cos A\sin B$ and $\cos(A \pm B) = \cos A\cos B \mp \sin A\sin B$

The sine formula keeps the sign; the cosine formula uses the **opposite** sign ($\mp$).

Watch out: $\sin(A + B) \ne \sin A + \sin B$.
Mnemonic: sine mixes (sin-cos, cos-sin) and keeps the sign; cosine matches (cos-cos, sin-sin) and flips it.
cards.searchQuery: sine cosine sum and difference formulas sin(A+B) cos(A-B)

cards.title: Use a difference formula to find the exact value of $\cos 15^\circ$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.966$

$\cos(45^\circ - 30^\circ) = \cos 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ + \sin 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}$.

Watch out: note the **plus** sign; $\cos(A - B)$ adds the sine product.
cards.searchQuery: exact value cos 15 degrees difference formula

cards.title: State the sum and difference formulas for $\tan(A \pm B)$.
cards.body:
$\tan(A \pm B) = \dfrac{\tan A \pm \tan B}{1 \mp \tan A\tan B}$

The numerator sign matches the operation; the denominator sign is the **opposite**.

Example: $\tan 75^\circ = \tan(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \frac{1 + \sqrt{3}/3}{1 - \sqrt{3}/3} = 2 + \sqrt{3}$.
cards.searchQuery: tangent sum and difference formula tan(A+B)

cards.title: $\cos\theta = -\frac{5}{13}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant III. Find the exact value of $\sin 2\theta$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{120}{169}$

$\sin\theta < 0$ in QIII, so $\sin\theta = -\sqrt{1 - \frac{25}{169}} = -\frac{12}{13}$. Then $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\frac{12}{13}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{13}\right) = \frac{120}{169}$.

Tip: sanity check: positive makes sense, since $2\theta$ lies between $2\pi$ and $3\pi$.
Watch out: forgetting the sign of $\sin\theta$ gives $-\frac{120}{169}$.
cards.searchQuery: sin 2 theta given cos theta quadrant III double angle

cards.title: Give all three forms of the double-angle formula for $\cos 2\theta$.
cards.body:
$\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$

The last two come from substituting $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$.

Tip: pick the form that uses what you know. Only $\cos\theta$ known: $2\cos^2\theta - 1$. Only $\sin\theta$ known: $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: cos 2 theta double angle formula three forms

cards.title: If $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{4}$, what is $\cos 2\theta$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{7}{8}$

Use the sine-only form: $\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta = 1 - 2\cdot\frac{1}{16} = 1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$.

Key idea: no quadrant information is needed, because only $\sin^2\theta$ appears.
cards.searchQuery: cos 2 theta from sin theta double angle value

cards.title: State the double-angle formula for $\tan 2\theta$ in terms of $\tan\theta$.
cards.body:
$\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$

It is the $\tan(A + B)$ formula with $A = B = \theta$.

Example: $\tan\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ gives $\tan 2\theta = \frac{1}{1 - 1/4} = \frac{4}{3}$.
cards.searchQuery: tan 2 theta double angle formula

cards.title: Power-reducing formulas: write $\sin^2\theta$ and $\cos^2\theta$ in terms of $\cos 2\theta$.
cards.body:
$\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}$ and $\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}$

They are the $\cos 2\theta$ formulas solved for $\sin^2\theta$ and $\cos^2\theta$. Replacing $\theta$ with $\frac{\theta}{2}$ gives the half-angle formulas.

Mnemonic: **sine** gets the **minus**.
cards.searchQuery: power reducing formulas sin squared cos squared

cards.title: In $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\theta}{2}}$, what decides the $\pm$ sign?
cards.body:
The quadrant of $\frac{\theta}{2}$, **not** the quadrant of $\theta$.

Example: $\theta = 300^\circ$ (QIV) gives $\frac{\theta}{2} = 150^\circ$ (QII), where sine is positive: $\sin 150^\circ = +\sqrt{\frac{1 - 1/2}{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Tip: the same rule holds for $\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\theta}{2}}$.
cards.searchQuery: half-angle formula sign quadrant of theta over 2

cards.title: Product-to-sum: rewrite $\sin A\cos B$ as a sum of sines.
cards.body:
$\sin A\cos B = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\right]$

Why: add the expansions of $\sin(A + B)$ and $\sin(A - B)$; the $\cos A\sin B$ terms cancel, leaving $2\sin A\cos B$.
cards.searchQuery: product to sum identity sin A cos B

cards.title: Write $\tan\theta$ and $\cot\theta$ in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$.
cards.body:
$\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$

These are the **quotient identities**. They are $\frac{y}{x}$ and $\frac{x}{y}$ for the unit-circle point $(x, y)$.

Tip: when a proof gets stuck, rewrite every function in terms of sine and cosine.
cards.searchQuery: quotient identities tangent cotangent sine cosine

cards.title: If $\sin\theta = -\frac{2}{3}$, what is $\csc\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{3}{2}$

$\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{1}{-2/3} = -\frac{3}{2}$.

Watch out: the reciprocal keeps the **sign**; it does not flip it.
cards.searchQuery: cosecant reciprocal of sine value

cards.title: If $\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\theta = -\frac{12}{13}$, what is $\tan\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{5}{12}$

$\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{5/13}{-12/13} = -\frac{5}{12}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\theta$ is in QII, where tangent is negative.
cards.searchQuery: tangent from sine and cosine quotient identity

cards.title: Why does $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ hold for every angle $\theta$?
cards.body:
The point $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ lies on the unit circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$, so substituting gives the identity.

For an acute angle it is also the **Pythagorean theorem** in a right triangle with hypotenuse $1$.

Key idea: every Pythagorean identity comes from this one by dividing through by $\sin^2\theta$ or $\cos^2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: why sin squared plus cos squared equals one unit circle

cards.title: Complete the Pythagorean identity: $\tan^2\theta + 1 = \,?$
cards.body:
$\sec^2\theta$

Divide $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ by $\cos^2\theta$: $\tan^2\theta + 1 = \sec^2\theta$.

Watch out: it is $\tan^2\theta + 1$, not $\tan^2\theta - 1$.
cards.searchQuery: tan squared plus 1 equals sec squared identity

cards.title: If $\sec\theta = -\frac{13}{5}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant II, what is $\tan\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{12}{5}$

$\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1 = \frac{169}{25} - 1 = \frac{144}{25}$, so $\tan\theta = \pm\frac{12}{5}$. Tangent is negative in QII.

Tip: this is a $5\text{-}12\text{-}13$ triangle with signs set by the quadrant.
cards.searchQuery: find tangent from secant quadrant II identity

cards.title: If $\cos\theta = -\frac{8}{17}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III, what is $\sin\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{15}{17}$

$\sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{64}{289} = \frac{225}{289}$, so $\sin\theta = \pm\frac{15}{17}$. Sine is negative in QIII.

Tip: recognize the $8\text{-}15\text{-}17$ triple to skip the arithmetic.
cards.searchQuery: find sine from cosine quadrant III Pythagorean

cards.title: If $\cot\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III, what is $\csc\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{5}{4}$

$\csc^2\theta = 1 + \cot^2\theta = 1 + \frac{9}{16} = \frac{25}{16}$, so $\csc\theta = \pm\frac{5}{4}$. Sine, and so cosecant, is negative in QIII.

Tip: sanity check: $\cot\theta > 0$ in QIII, which is consistent.
cards.searchQuery: find cosecant from cotangent quadrant III identity

cards.title: Simplify $\dfrac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta}$ for $\sin\theta \ne 0$.
cards.body:
$\sin\theta$

$1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$, so the fraction is $\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta} = \sin\theta$.

Tip: $1 - \cos^2\theta$ and $1 - \sin^2\theta$ are the two rearrangements of the Pythagorean identity.
cards.searchQuery: simplify 1 minus cos squared over sin

cards.title: Simplify $\sec^2\theta - 1$.
cards.body:
$\tan^2\theta$

Rearrange $\tan^2\theta + 1 = \sec^2\theta$.

Watch out: it is $\tan^2\theta$, not $\tan\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: simplify sec squared minus 1 tan squared

cards.title: Simplify $(1 - \sin\theta)(1 + \sin\theta)$.
cards.body:
$\cos^2\theta$

It is a difference of squares: $1 - \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta$.

Tip: this product is why multiplying by $1 + \sin\theta$ (a **conjugate**) clears $1 - \sin\theta$ from a denominator.
cards.searchQuery: simplify (1 - sin)(1 + sin) difference of squares

cards.title: Simplify $\tan\theta\cos\theta$.
cards.body:
$\sin\theta$

$\tan\theta\cos\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\cos\theta = \sin\theta$.

Tip: rewrite in sine and cosine, then cancel.
cards.searchQuery: simplify tan theta cos theta

cards.title: Which of the six trig functions are even, and which are odd?
cards.body:
**Even**: $\cos$ and $\sec$. **Odd**: $\sin$, $\csc$, $\tan$ and $\cot$.

Even means $f(-\theta) = f(\theta)$; odd means $f(-\theta) = -f(\theta)$.

Mnemonic: cosine is the only "co" that is even, and its reciprocal secant goes with it.
cards.searchQuery: even and odd trig functions list

cards.title: Exact value of $\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{2}$

Cosine is **even**: $\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Key idea: for an **even** function, $f(-x) = f(x)$, so the sign of the angle drops out.
cards.searchQuery: cos of negative pi/3 even function

cards.title: Exact value of $\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{1}{2}$

Sine is **odd**: $\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: $-\frac{\pi}{6}$ ends in QIV, where sine is negative.
cards.searchQuery: sin of negative pi/6 odd function

cards.title: Exact value of $\tan(-60^\circ)$?
cards.body:
$-\sqrt{3}$

Tangent is **odd**: $\tan(-60^\circ) = -\tan 60^\circ = -\sqrt{3}$.
Tip: for an **odd** function, pull the minus sign out front.
cards.searchQuery: tan of negative 60 degrees odd

cards.title: Why is cosine even but sine odd, in terms of the unit circle?
cards.body:
Replacing $\theta$ by $-\theta$ **reflects** the terminal point across the $x$-axis, from $(x, y)$ to $(x, -y)$.

The $x$-coordinate (cosine) stays the same, so cosine is even. The $y$-coordinate (sine) changes sign, so sine is odd. Tangent $\frac{y}{x}$ flips sign, so it is odd.
Mnemonic: cosine is the $x$-coordinate, and a reflection across the $x$-axis leaves $x$ alone.
cards.searchQuery: why cosine even sine odd unit circle reflection

cards.title: Simplify $\cos(-x)\tan(-x)$.
cards.body:
$-\sin x$

$\cos(-x) = \cos x$ and $\tan(-x) = -\tan x$, so the product is $-\cos x\cdot\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = -\sin x$.
Tip: remove the negative angles first, then simplify.
cards.searchQuery: simplify cos(-x) tan(-x) even odd

cards.title: Cofunction identity: $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \,?$
cards.body:
$\cos\theta$

The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its **complement**. That is where the name "cosine" comes from.

Example: $\sin 60^\circ = \cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
cards.searchQuery: cofunction identity sin pi/2 minus theta equals cos

cards.title: $\sin 70^\circ = \cos x^\circ$ with $x$ acute. Find $x$.
cards.body:
$20$

$\sin\theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta)$, so $\sin 70^\circ = \cos 20^\circ$.

Watch out: complementary angles sum to $90^\circ$, not $180^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: sin 70 equals cos of complement degrees

cards.title: If $\sin 3x = \cos 2x$ with $x$ acute (in degrees), find $x$.
cards.body:
$18^\circ$

$\cos 2x = \sin(90^\circ - 2x)$, so $3x = 90^\circ - 2x$ and $x = 18^\circ$.

Tip: sanity check: $\sin 54^\circ = \cos 36^\circ$ (both $\approx 0.809$).
Tip: for acute angles, $\sin A = \cos B$ means $A + B = 90^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: solve sin 3x = cos 2x acute angle cofunction

cards.title: Cofunction identity: $\sec\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \,?$
cards.body:
$\csc\theta$

$\sec\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \frac{1}{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)} = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \csc\theta$.

Key idea: the three cofunction pairs are sin-cos, tan-cot and sec-csc.
cards.searchQuery: cofunction identity sec pi/2 minus theta equals csc

cards.title: Exact value of $\sin 75^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}$

$\sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.966$.

Tip: sanity check: $\sin 75^\circ = \cos 15^\circ$, the same value as in the earlier card.
cards.searchQuery: exact value sin 75 degrees sum formula

cards.title: Exact value of $\cos 75^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}$

$\cos(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \cos 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ - \sin 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\approx 0.259$, small because $75^\circ$ is close to $90^\circ$.
Watch out: the sum formula for cosine has a **minus** sign.
cards.searchQuery: exact value cos 75 degrees sum formula

cards.title: Exact value of $\tan 15^\circ$?
cards.body:
$2 - \sqrt{3}$

$\tan(45^\circ - 30^\circ) = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}/3}{1 + \sqrt{3}/3} = \frac{3 - \sqrt{3}}{3 + \sqrt{3}} = \frac{(3 - \sqrt{3})^2}{6} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\approx 0.268$, and $\tan 75^\circ = 2 + \sqrt{3}$ is its reciprocal.
cards.searchQuery: exact value tan 15 degrees difference formula

cards.title: Exact value of $\sin\frac{\pi}{12}$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}$

$\frac{\pi}{12} = 15^\circ = 45^\circ - 30^\circ$, so $\sin 15^\circ = \sin 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ - \cos 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.259$.

Tip: $\sin 15^\circ = \cos 75^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: exact value sin pi/12 15 degrees

cards.title: Exact value of $\cos 105^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4}$

$\cos(60^\circ + 45^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4} \approx -0.259$.

Tip: sanity check: $105^\circ$ is in QII, so the cosine is negative.
cards.searchQuery: exact value cos 105 degrees sum formula

cards.title: Evaluate $\sin 20^\circ\cos 10^\circ + \cos 20^\circ\sin 10^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{2}$

It is the right side of $\sin(A + B)$ with $A = 20^\circ$ and $B = 10^\circ$, so it equals $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$.

Tip: spot the pattern in reverse; many exam problems hide a sum formula.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate sin 20 cos 10 plus cos 20 sin 10

cards.title: Evaluate $\cos 80^\circ\cos 20^\circ + \sin 80^\circ\sin 20^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{2}$

The plus sign marks $\cos(A - B)$ with $A = 80^\circ$ and $B = 20^\circ$: $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$.

Watch out: with a **plus** between the products it is $\cos(A - B)$, not $\cos(A + B)$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate cos 80 cos 20 plus sin 80 sin 20

cards.title: Evaluate $\dfrac{\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ}{1 - \tan 20^\circ\tan 25^\circ}$ exactly.
cards.body:
$1$

It matches $\tan(A + B)$ with $A = 20^\circ$ and $B = 25^\circ$, so it equals $\tan 45^\circ = 1$.
Tip: recognize the $\tan(A + B)$ pattern before computing any tangent values.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate tan 20 plus tan 25 over 1 minus product

cards.title: $\sin A = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos B = \frac{5}{13}$ with $A$ and $B$ both acute. Find $\cos(A + B)$.
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{16}{65}$

Acute angles give $\cos A = \frac{4}{5}$ and $\sin B = \frac{12}{13}$. Then $\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B = \frac{20}{65} - \frac{36}{65} = -\frac{16}{65}$.

Tip: sanity check: $A \approx 36.9^\circ$ and $B \approx 67.4^\circ$ sum to about $104^\circ$, so the cosine is slightly negative.
cards.searchQuery: cos(A+B) given sin A and cos B acute angles

cards.title: $\sin A = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos B = \frac{5}{13}$ with $A$ and $B$ both acute. Find $\sin(A + B)$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{63}{65}$

With $\cos A = \frac{4}{5}$ and $\sin B = \frac{12}{13}$: $\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B = \frac{15}{65} + \frac{48}{65} = \frac{63}{65}$.

Tip: sanity check: the angle is about $104^\circ$, whose sine is about $0.97$.
cards.searchQuery: sin(A+B) given sin A and cos B acute angles

cards.title: If $\tan A = 2$ and $\tan B = 3$, what is $\tan(A + B)$?
cards.body:
$-1$

$\tan(A + B) = \frac{2 + 3}{1 - 2\cdot 3} = \frac{5}{-5} = -1$.

Tip: sanity check: $A + B \approx 63.4^\circ + 71.6^\circ = 135^\circ$, and $\tan 135^\circ = -1$.
cards.searchQuery: tan(A+B) given tan A and tan B

cards.title: Simplify $\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
cards.body:
$\cos x$

$\sin x\cos\frac{\pi}{2} + \cos x\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = \sin x\cdot 0 + \cos x\cdot 1 = \cos x$.

Key idea: shifting sine left by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ turns it into cosine.
cards.searchQuery: sin(x + pi/2) simplify cos x

cards.title: Simplify $\cos(x + \pi)$.
cards.body:
$-\cos x$

$\cos x\cos\pi - \sin x\sin\pi = -\cos x$.

Why: adding $\pi$ is a half-turn, which negates both coordinates of the point.
cards.searchQuery: cos(x + pi) simplify negative cosine

cards.title: Simplify $\sin(\pi - x)$.
cards.body:
$\sin x$

$\sin\pi\cos x - \cos\pi\sin x = 0 - (-1)\sin x = \sin x$.

Watch out: $\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x$; only sine keeps its sign.
cards.searchQuery: sin(pi - x) simplify supplementary angle

cards.title: Is $\sin(A + B) = \sin A + \sin B$ always true? Give a counterexample.
cards.body:
**No.** Take $A = B = \frac{\pi}{2}$ (radians): $\sin(A + B) = \sin\pi = 0$, but $\sin A + \sin B = 1 + 1 = 2$.

Sine does not **distribute** over addition, and neither do the other trig functions. The correct rule is $\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$.

Watch out: the same trap applies to $\cos(A + B)$ and $\tan(A + B)$.
cards.searchQuery: sin(A+B) does not equal sin A plus sin B

cards.title: Why does the formula for $\cos(A - B)$ come from the unit circle?
cards.body:
Take the points $P = (\cos A, \sin A)$ and $Q = (\cos B, \sin B)$. Their squared distance expands to $2 - 2(\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B)$.

Rotating the picture so $Q$ sits at $(1, 0)$ gives the same chord, with squared length $2 - 2\cos(A - B)$. Equating the two gives $\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$.

Key idea: rotation does not change distance. The other sum and difference formulas follow from this one.
cards.searchQuery: derive cos(A-B) formula unit circle distance

cards.title: State the double-angle formula for sine.
cards.body:
$\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$

It is $\sin(A + B)$ with $A = B = \theta$: $\sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos\theta\sin\theta$.

Watch out: $\sin 2\theta \ne 2\sin\theta$; try $\theta = 30^\circ$: $\sin 60^\circ \approx 0.866$ but $2\sin 30^\circ = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: sin 2 theta double angle formula

cards.title: If $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ with $\theta$ acute, find $\sin 2\theta$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{24}{25}$

A $3\text{-}4\text{-}5$ triangle gives $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}$, so $\sin 2\theta = 2\cdot\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{4}{5} = \frac{24}{25}$.

Tip: draw the right triangle first when you are given a tangent.
cards.searchQuery: sin 2 theta from tan theta acute

cards.title: If $\cos\theta = \frac{3}{5}$, what is $\cos 2\theta$?
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{7}{25}$

Use $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 2\cdot\frac{9}{25} - 1 = -\frac{7}{25}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\theta \approx 53.1^\circ$, so $2\theta \approx 106.3^\circ$, which is in QII, so cosine is negative.
cards.searchQuery: cos 2 theta from cos theta double angle value

cards.title: If $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$, what is $\tan 2\theta$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{24}{7}$

$\tan 2\theta = \frac{2\cdot\frac{3}{4}}{1 - \frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3/2}{7/16} = \frac{24}{7}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\sin 2\theta = \frac{24}{25}$ and $\cos 2\theta = \frac{7}{25}$ for acute $\theta$, whose ratio is $\frac{24}{7}$.
cards.searchQuery: tan 2 theta from tan theta value 3/4

cards.title: Evaluate $2\sin 15^\circ\cos 15^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{2}$

$2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \sin 2\theta$, so this is $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$.
Tip: $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ is a **double angle** in disguise.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate 2 sin 15 cos 15 double angle

cards.title: Evaluate $\cos^2 22.5^\circ - \sin^2 22.5^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$

$\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$, so this is $\cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
Tip: a difference of squares of cosine and sine is $\cos 2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate cos squared 22.5 minus sin squared 22.5

cards.title: Evaluate $\dfrac{2\tan 15^\circ}{1 - \tan^2 15^\circ}$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$

It matches $\tan 2\theta$ with $\theta = 15^\circ$, so it equals $\tan 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Tip: $\frac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$ is the $\tan 2\theta$ pattern.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate 2 tan 15 over 1 minus tan squared 15

cards.title: Evaluate $1 - 2\sin^2\frac{\pi}{12}$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$1 - 2\sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$, so with $\theta = \frac{\pi}{12}$ this is $\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
Tip: $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ is one of the three forms of $\cos 2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate 1 minus 2 sin squared pi/12

cards.title: State the half-angle formulas for $\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$ and $\tan\frac{\theta}{2}$.
cards.body:
$\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \cos\theta}{2}}$ and $\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{1 + \cos\theta} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$

The $\pm$ is set by the quadrant of $\frac{\theta}{2}$. The two tangent forms need **no** sign choice.

Mnemonic: cosine gets the **plus** under the root; sine gets the minus.
cards.searchQuery: half-angle formulas cosine tangent

cards.title: Exact value of $\cos 22.5^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2} \approx 0.924$

$22.5^\circ$ is half of $45^\circ$ and lies in QI, so $\cos 22.5^\circ = +\sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos 45^\circ}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sqrt{2}/2}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: it should be a bit under $\cos 0 = 1$ and above $\cos 45^\circ \approx 0.707$.
cards.searchQuery: exact value cos 22.5 degrees half angle

cards.title: Exact value of $\tan 22.5^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\sqrt{2} - 1 \approx 0.414$

$\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{\sin\theta}{1 + \cos\theta}$ with $\theta = 45^\circ$: $\frac{\sqrt{2}/2}{1 + \sqrt{2}/2} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 + \sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} - 1$ after rationalizing.

Tip: the sine-over-one-plus-cosine form avoids a square root and a sign choice.
cards.searchQuery: exact value tan 22.5 degrees half angle

cards.title: $\cos\theta = -\frac{7}{25}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant II. Find $\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{3}{5}$

$\theta$ is between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$, so $\frac{\theta}{2}$ is between $45^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ (QI), and cosine is positive. Then $\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - 7/25}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} = \frac{3}{5}$.

Key idea: halving the angle halves its quadrant range.
cards.searchQuery: cos theta over 2 given cos theta quadrant II half angle

cards.title: $\cos\theta = -\frac{7}{25}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant II. Find $\sin\frac{\theta}{2}$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{4}{5}$

$\frac{\theta}{2}$ is in QI, so sine is positive: $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 7/25}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}} = \frac{4}{5}$.

Tip: sanity check: with the earlier card, $\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: sin theta over 2 given cos theta quadrant II half angle

cards.title: $\cos\theta = -\frac{7}{25}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant II. Find $\tan\frac{\theta}{2}$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{4}{3}$

In QII, $\sin\theta = \frac{24}{25}$. Then $\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{\sin\theta}{1 + \cos\theta} = \frac{24/25}{18/25} = \frac{4}{3}$.

Tip: sanity check: it equals $\frac{\sin(\theta/2)}{\cos(\theta/2)} = \frac{4/5}{3/5}$.
cards.searchQuery: tan theta over 2 given cos theta quadrant II

cards.title: How do the half-angle formulas follow from the double-angle formulas?
cards.body:
Start from $\cos 2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\alpha$ and solve for $\sin^2\alpha$: $\sin^2\alpha = \frac{1 - \cos 2\alpha}{2}$. Now let $\alpha = \frac{\theta}{2}$, so $2\alpha = \theta$.

Taking square roots gives $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\theta}{2}}$. The $\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1$ form gives the cosine formula the same way.

Key idea: half-angle formulas are **power-reducing formulas** with $\theta$ renamed.
cards.searchQuery: derive half angle formula from double angle

cards.title: Exact value of $\sin^2 15^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{3}}{4}$

Use $\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}$: $\frac{1 - \cos 30^\circ}{2} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}/2}{2} = \frac{2 - \sqrt{3}}{4} \approx 0.067$.

Tip: sanity check: $\sin 15^\circ \approx 0.259$, and $0.259^2 \approx 0.067$.
cards.searchQuery: exact value sin squared 15 degrees power reducing

cards.title: Write $\sin^4 x$ using only first powers of cosines of multiples of $x$.
cards.body:
$\sin^4 x = \dfrac{3 - 4\cos 2x + \cos 4x}{8}$

Square the power-reducing formula: $\sin^4 x = \left(\frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1 - 2\cos 2x + \cos^2 2x}{4}$. Then reduce $\cos^2 2x = \frac{1 + \cos 4x}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: at $x = 0$ both sides are $0$, and at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ both are $1$.
Tip: repeat the power-reducing step until no powers remain; this is how you prepare integrals.
cards.searchQuery: power reduction sin to the fourth x formula

cards.title: If $\cos 2\theta = \frac{1}{3}$ with $\theta$ acute, find $\cos\theta$.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{3}$

$\cos^2\theta = \frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2} = \frac{4/3}{2} = \frac{2}{3}$. For acute $\theta$ cosine is positive, so $\cos\theta = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3} \approx 0.816$.

Watch out: $\cos\theta \ne \frac{1}{6}$; halving the angle does not halve the cosine.
cards.searchQuery: cos theta from cos 2 theta acute power reducing

cards.title: What is the average value of $\sin^2 x$ over one full period?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\sin^2 x = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}$, and $\cos 2x$ averages to $0$ over a period, leaving $\frac{1}{2}$.

Key idea: $\sin^2 x$ and $\cos^2 x$ both oscillate around $\frac{1}{2}$ and sum to $1$ at every $x$.
cards.searchQuery: average value of sin squared over one period

cards.title: Express $\cos 3\theta$ in terms of $\cos\theta$.
cards.body:
$\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$

Write $\cos 3\theta = \cos(2\theta + \theta) = \cos 2\theta\cos\theta - \sin 2\theta\sin\theta$. Substitute $2\cos^2\theta - 1$ and $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$, then replace $\sin^2\theta$ by $1 - \cos^2\theta$.

Tip: sanity check: $\theta = 0$ gives $4 - 3 = 1$, and $\theta = 60^\circ$ gives $4\cdot\frac{1}{8} - \frac{3}{2} = -1 = \cos 180^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: triple angle formula cos 3 theta

cards.title: Express $\sin 3\theta$ in terms of $\sin\theta$.
cards.body:
$\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$

Write $\sin 3\theta = \sin(2\theta + \theta) = \sin 2\theta\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta\sin\theta$ and substitute the double-angle formulas.

Tip: sanity check: $\theta = 30^\circ$ gives $\frac{3}{2} - 4\cdot\frac{1}{8} = 1 = \sin 90^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: triple angle formula sin 3 theta

cards.title: Product-to-sum: rewrite $\cos A\cos B$ as a sum of cosines.
cards.body:
$\cos A\cos B = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B)\right]$

Why: add $\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$ and $\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B$; the sine terms cancel.
cards.searchQuery: product to sum identity cos A cos B

cards.title: Product-to-sum: rewrite $\sin A\sin B$ as a sum of cosines.
cards.body:
$\sin A\sin B = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos(A - B) - \cos(A + B)\right]$

Why: **subtract** $\cos(A + B)$ from $\cos(A - B)$; the cosine terms cancel and $2\sin A\sin B$ remains.

Watch out: the order is $A - B$ first, then $A + B$; reversing it flips the sign.
cards.searchQuery: product to sum identity sin A sin B

cards.title: Product-to-sum: rewrite $\cos A\sin B$ as a sum of sines.
cards.body:
$\cos A\sin B = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\sin(A + B) - \sin(A - B)\right]$

Why: subtract the expansions of $\sin(A - B)$ from $\sin(A + B)$; the $\sin A\cos B$ terms cancel.

Tip: you rarely need to memorize this; swap $A$ and $B$ in the $\sin A\cos B$ formula.
cards.searchQuery: product to sum identity cos A sin B

cards.title: Sum-to-product: rewrite $\sin A + \sin B$ as a product.
cards.body:
$\sin A + \sin B = 2\sin\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2}$

Why: in $\sin x\cos y = \frac{1}{2}[\sin(x + y) + \sin(x - y)]$, set $x = \frac{A + B}{2}$ and $y = \frac{A - B}{2}$.

Example: $\sin 75^\circ + \sin 15^\circ = 2\sin 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ$.
cards.searchQuery: sum to product identity sin A plus sin B

cards.title: Sum-to-product: rewrite $\cos A + \cos B$ as a product.
cards.body:
$\cos A + \cos B = 2\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2}$

Why: set $x = \frac{A + B}{2}$ and $y = \frac{A - B}{2}$ in $\cos x\cos y = \frac{1}{2}[\cos(x - y) + \cos(x + y)]$.

Watch out: the difference version is $\cos A - \cos B = -2\sin\frac{A + B}{2}\sin\frac{A - B}{2}$, with a minus sign out front.
cards.searchQuery: sum to product identity cos A plus cos B

cards.title: Sum-to-product: rewrite $\cos A - \cos B$ as a product.
cards.body:
$\cos A - \cos B = -2\sin\dfrac{A + B}{2}\sin\dfrac{A - B}{2}$

Why: it comes from $\sin x\sin y = \frac{1}{2}[\cos(x - y) - \cos(x + y)]$ with $x = \frac{A + B}{2}$ and $y = \frac{A - B}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: $A = 0$ and $B = 90^\circ$ gives $1 - 0 = 1$, and $-2\sin 45^\circ\sin(-45^\circ) = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: sum to product identity cos A minus cos B

cards.title: Sum-to-product: rewrite $\sin A - \sin B$ as a product.
cards.body:
$\sin A - \sin B = 2\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\sin\dfrac{A - B}{2}$

Why: it comes from $\cos x\sin y = \frac{1}{2}[\sin(x + y) - \sin(x - y)]$ with $x = \frac{A + B}{2}$ and $y = \frac{A - B}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: $A = 90^\circ$ and $B = 0$ gives $1$, and $2\cos 45^\circ\sin 45^\circ = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: sum to product identity sin A minus sin B

cards.title: Evaluate $\sin 75^\circ + \sin 15^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$2\sin\frac{75^\circ + 15^\circ}{2}\cos\frac{75^\circ - 15^\circ}{2} = 2\sin 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ = 2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \approx 1.225$.

Tip: sanity check: $0.966 + 0.259 \approx 1.225$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate sin 75 plus sin 15 sum to product

cards.title: Evaluate $\cos 75^\circ\cos 15^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{1}{4}$

$\cos A\cos B = \frac{1}{2}[\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B)] = \frac{1}{2}[\cos 60^\circ + \cos 90^\circ] = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$.

Shortcut: $\cos 75^\circ = \sin 15^\circ$, so this is $\sin 15^\circ\cos 15^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\sin 30^\circ$.
Tip: complementary angles let you swap cosine for sine and use the double-angle formula.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate cos 75 cos 15 product to sum

cards.title: Evaluate $\sin 105^\circ\cos 15^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{3}}{4}$

$\sin A\cos B = \frac{1}{2}[\sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)] = \frac{1}{2}[\sin 120^\circ + \sin 90^\circ] = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 1\right) = \frac{2 + \sqrt{3}}{4}$.

Tip: sanity check: $0.966 \times 0.966 \approx 0.933$, and $\frac{2 + 1.732}{4} \approx 0.933$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate sin 105 cos 15 product to sum

cards.title: Evaluate $\cos 75^\circ - \cos 15^\circ$ exactly.
cards.body:
$-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$

$-2\sin\frac{75^\circ + 15^\circ}{2}\sin\frac{75^\circ - 15^\circ}{2} = -2\sin 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ = -2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: $0.259 - 0.966 \approx -0.707$.
cards.searchQuery: evaluate cos 75 minus cos 15 sum to product

cards.title: Write $\sin 2\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta$ in terms of $\tan\theta$.
cards.body:
$\sin 2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta}$ and $\cos 2\theta = \dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta}$

Why: divide numerator and denominator of $\frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta}$ by $\cos^2\theta$.

Tip: sanity check: $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ gives $\frac{3/2}{25/16} = \frac{24}{25}$, matching $\sin 2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: sin 2 theta cos 2 theta in terms of tan theta

cards.title: Prove that $\sec\theta - \cos\theta = \sin\theta\tan\theta$.
cards.body:
Start with the left side and write it over a common denominator: $\frac{1}{\cos\theta} - \cos\theta = \frac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

Split it as $\sin\theta \cdot \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \sin\theta\tan\theta$, which is the right side.

Tip: convert to sine and cosine, **combine fractions**, then use $1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$.
cards.searchQuery: prove identity sec theta minus cos theta

cards.title: Prove that $\tan x + \cot x = \sec x\csc x$.
cards.body:
Write the left side in sines and cosines and add: $\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x\cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x\cos x}$.

That is $\frac{1}{\cos x}\cdot\frac{1}{\sin x} = \sec x\csc x$.

Key idea: the **Pythagorean identity** turns the numerator into $1$.
cards.searchQuery: prove identity tan x plus cot x equals sec x csc x

cards.title: Simplify $\sin x(\csc x - \sin x)$.
cards.body:
$\cos^2 x$

Distribute: $\sin x\csc x - \sin^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x$.
Tip: $\sin x\csc x = 1$, since they are reciprocals.
cards.searchQuery: simplify sin x times csc x minus sin x

cards.title: Simplify $\dfrac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \dfrac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}$.
cards.body:
$2\sec x$

Common denominator: $\frac{\cos^2 x + (1 + \sin x)^2}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{2 + 2\sin x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{2}{\cos x}$.

Tip: expand and use $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$; the factor $1 + \sin x$ then cancels.
cards.searchQuery: simplify cos x over 1 plus sin x plus 1 plus sin x over cos x

cards.title: Simplify $\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sin x}$ for $\sin x \ne 0$.
cards.body:
$2\cos x$

$\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\sin x} = 2\cos x$.
Watch out: you may cancel $\sin x$ only because $\sin x \ne 0$.
cards.searchQuery: simplify sin 2x over sin x

cards.title: Simplify $\dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{\sin 2x}$ where it is defined.
cards.body:
$\tan x$

Use $1 - \cos 2x = 2\sin^2 x$ and $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$: $\frac{2\sin^2 x}{2\sin x\cos x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x$.

Tip: choose the double-angle form of $\cos 2x$ that cancels the constant $1$.
cards.searchQuery: simplify 1 minus cos 2x over sin 2x tan x

cards.title: Simplify $\sin x\cos x(\tan x + \cot x)$.
cards.body:
$1$

Since $\tan x + \cot x = \frac{1}{\sin x\cos x}$, the product is $\sin x\cos x \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x\cos x} = 1$.

Tip: sanity check: at $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$, $\frac{1}{2}(1 + 1) = 1$.
cards.searchQuery: simplify sin x cos x times tan x plus cot x

cards.title: What is the difference between a trig identity and a conditional equation, such as $\sin\theta = \cos\theta$?
cards.body:
An **identity** is true for every angle where both sides are defined. A **conditional equation** is true only for certain angles.

Example: $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ is an identity, but $\sin\theta = \cos\theta$ holds only at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{4} + k\pi$ (radians).

Tip: you prove an identity, but you solve an equation.
cards.searchQuery: trig identity versus conditional equation difference

cards.title: Is $\tan\theta\cot\theta = 1$ true for every real $\theta$?
cards.body:
**No.** It holds only where both functions are defined. At $\theta = 0$, $\cot\theta$ is undefined, and at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$, $\tan\theta$ is undefined.

Identities are statements about the values where both sides make sense.

Watch out: cancelling a factor such as $\sin\theta$ silently assumes it is not zero.
cards.searchQuery: is tan theta cot theta equal to 1 domain restrictions

cards.title: How can you quickly show that a proposed trig identity is false?
cards.body:
Substitute **one** convenient angle where both sides are defined and show they differ. One counterexample is enough.

Example: to test $\sin 2x = 2\sin x$, use $x = 30^\circ$: $\sin 60^\circ \approx 0.866$, but $2\sin 30^\circ = 1$.

Watch out: agreement at one angle does not prove an identity; it only fails to disprove it.
cards.searchQuery: counterexample to disprove trig identity test value

cards.title: Simplify $\sin(A + B)\sin(A - B)$ in terms of $\sin A$ and $\sin B$.
cards.body:
$\sin^2 A - \sin^2 B$

Expand: $(\sin A\cos B)^2 - (\cos A\sin B)^2 = \sin^2 A(1 - \sin^2 B) - (1 - \sin^2 A)\sin^2 B = \sin^2 A - \sin^2 B$.

Tip: sanity check: $A = 90^\circ$ and $B = 30^\circ$ give $\sin 120^\circ\sin 60^\circ = \frac{3}{4}$ and $1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$.
cards.searchQuery: sin(A+B) sin(A-B) equals sin squared A minus sin squared B

cards.title: Simplify $\cos(A + B)\cos(A - B)$ in terms of $\cos A$ and $\sin B$.
cards.body:
$\cos^2 A - \sin^2 B$

Expand: $\cos^2 A\cos^2 B - \sin^2 A\sin^2 B = \cos^2 A(1 - \sin^2 B) - (1 - \cos^2 A)\sin^2 B = \cos^2 A - \sin^2 B$.

Tip: sanity check: $A = 0$ and $B = 90^\circ$ give $\cos 90^\circ\cos(-90^\circ) = 0$ and $1 - 1 = 0$.
cards.searchQuery: cos(A+B) cos(A-B) equals cos squared A minus sin squared B

cards.title: Exact value of $\sin 22.5^\circ$?
cards.body:
$\dfrac{\sqrt{2 - \sqrt{2}}}{2} \approx 0.383$

$22.5^\circ$ is half of $45^\circ$ and lies in QI, so $\sin 22.5^\circ = +\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos 45^\circ}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \sqrt{2}/2}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2 - \sqrt{2}}}{2}$.

Tip: sanity check: $\sin^2 22.5^\circ + \cos^2 22.5^\circ = \frac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{4} + \frac{2 + \sqrt{2}}{4} = 1$.
Watch out: the minus under the root belongs to **sine**; cosine gets the plus.
cards.searchQuery: exact value sin 22.5 degrees half angle
